title: tier-2 shipped code: the key-state range resolve against DynamicIndexResolveRange (0x1425115d0)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/index.rs::resolve_range, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the dynamic_index_resolve_range entry. The ledger binds the verdict to index.rs + the probe source + the git revision. Production's SegmentEntries::resolve_range looks the key up and calls the same KeyState::resolve body, so the shipped path and the tested function share the arithmetic; the wrapper adds the client's own prologue and status mapping (2 no entry, 3 not resident, 4 past the end, 0 found).

Oracle is DynamicIndexResolveRange at exe 0x1425115d0, extent 0x1425115d0..0x1425116f2 (291 bytes through the ret at 0x1425116f1; the .pdata root is only 0x1425115d0..0x1425115ee, 0x1e bytes, and the body continues past it, with no tail jump - the exit is the cookie check through 0x1426c3d40 and the ret), which is the declared coverageWindow. v2b 0x7ff7c72315d0 is 0x7ff7c4d20000 + (0x1425115d0 - 0x140000000). Signature: (segment *segment, const key[9] *key, request *request, range *out_range, chosen *out_entry) -> u8 status (RCX, RDX, R8, R9, then the stack argument).

The read, in order: DynamicIndexFindContextInit (0x142520520) builds the key state on the client's own stack from the segment's [0] and [8]; DynamicIndexFindEntry (0x1425111a0) is called with both out words null and fills found at +0x10, the chosen entry at +0x18 and the interval buffer at +0x28. A zero found byte returns 2 (0x1425111634). The request's start is compared against the chosen entry's stored size (the u32 at +8, zero-extended) - greater returns 4 (0x142511165f); a length of 0xffffffff becomes size - start in 32-bit arithmetic (0x1425111668); start + len beyond the size returns 4 (0x1425111676). The out range is then written (the u32 length at +8, the absolute chosen.location + start at +0, 0x1425111680/0x1425111687) BEFORE the resident check, a zero length skips that check (0x142511168a), and DynamicIndexRangeIsResident (0x142520c60) with flag 1 answers it - false returns 3 (0x14251116a0). On success the 16-byte chosen entry is written when the out pointer is non-null (0x14251116ae), the context is freed (0x142520570) and the status is the zero `esi` was seeded with at 0x142511161a.

Compared channels: the return byte (AL) and one 0x6000-byte blob holding the segment at 0 (entries base, entry count, page-table base, page count, logger), the allocator slot at 0x1000, the 18-byte entries at 0x3000, the 24-byte page records at 0x4000, the disabled logger at 0x5200, the key at 0x5600, the 16-byte request at 0x5700, the out range at 0x5800 and the out entry at 0x5900 - both out regions sentinel-filled, so the client's three stores and their exact widths are all visible. The probe writes the range only for status 0 and 3 and the entry only for status 0 when the pointer is non-null, which is where the client writes them.

The fixture's declared cases walk every status: 2 from an empty entry array, a key the walk cannot find, a page record of type 3, and a null out entry; 4 from start past the size, start + len past it, start 0xffffffff, and a zero stored size with a non-empty request; 0 from a resident prefix, the whole entry, the empty range, the last byte, a start at the far end, and the 0xffffffff length form that resolves to the entry's end; 3 from a type-5 page record that clears the interval buffer (with its zero-length companion, which skips the check and succeeds). The type 2/4/6/7 page records are pinned separately; distinct interval starts keep the unstable normalize sort's order unique. The sweep afterwards varies the entry count and location, the page record types and the request's start and length, including both 0xffffffff forms.

Coverage: the 291-byte window holds seven conditional branch sites - the found test, the two past-the-end tests, the 0xffffffff length test, the zero-length test, the resident test and the null out-entry test. All seven are driven to both edges by the declared cases, so the gate is 100%.

acknowledgedGaps.what: the interval-buffer grow inside the lookup
acknowledgedGaps.why: DynamicIndexFindEntry appends through DynamicIndexAppendInterval, whose capacity grow (log 0x1424f8440 + the allocator vtable at [segment]) is the declared gap of fn/DynamicIndexFindEntry and fn/DynamicIndexAppendInterval. The fixture keeps equal entries plus page matches at eight or fewer against the fresh state's capacity of 16 (the probe rejects more).

acknowledgedGaps.what: the pointer-array grow past 32 page matches
acknowledgedGaps.why: The same allocator-vtable growth fn/DynamicIndexFindEntry declares: every case keeps matches <= 32 and the probe rejects more.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a context free that has left the inline buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: DynamicIndexFindContextFree (0x142520570) only calls the allocator vtable when the interval base is not the inline buffer at ctx+0x28, which needs the grow above. With no grow it is the compare and the ret, so the readable path is proved and the free-through-vtable path stays open.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a type 4/5 log call with a live logger
acknowledgedGaps.why: The sink's type 4 and 5 branches call the log function at 0x1424f8440 with the logger at [ctx+8] (the segment's +8 word). The fixture's logger has level 0 at its +8, so the call returns after its cookie checks; a live logger's output is outside the system.

acknowledgedGaps.what: equal interval starts in one pre-normalize buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client's sort (0x14251ff30) is unstable, so two events with the same start can be ordered either way; every fixture case keeps all appended starts distinct.
